backward_compat_traps.rule: A DDR5 DIMM has TWO independent 32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating a DDR5 DIMM as a single 64/72-bit DDR4 bus is wrong.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR5 native burst length is 16 (DDR4 is 8).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming BL8 mis-sizes the 64-byte access on a 32-bit sub-channel.

backward_compat_traps.rule: VrefDQ/VrefCA are generated on-die and trained.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Supplying an external VrefDQ as in older parts is wrong.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR5 commands occupy two CA cycles.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Decoding DDR5 commands as single-cycle DDR4 commands is wrong.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR5 is the mainstream generation timed off CK/DQS with no WCK and no TSV stacking; LPDDR5 has a WCK and is low-power, HBM3 is 3D-stacked (TSV, 1024-bit, pseudo-channels).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Applying LPDDR5 WCK or HBM3 stacked/pseudo-channel assumptions to DDR5 is wrong.

spec_lineage_lpddr.summary: Original low-power DDR; 1.8 V; temperature-compensated / partial-array self-refresh; deep power-down.
1.2 V; 2n/4n prefetch + non-volatile option; 10-bit DDR CA bus; up to LPDDR2-1066.
1600 MT/s; write-leveling, CA training, optional ODT; 8n prefetch.
Two 16-bit channels; 6-bit CA bus (two-cycle commands, CS active-high, no CKE); 16n prefetch; DBI; up to 3200 MT/s. LPDDR4X reduces Vddq to 0.6 V.

WCK / RDQS on-demand clocking with quarter-speed CK; 7-bit DDR CA bus; 16 banks in 4 bank groups; 16n prefetch; VDDQ 0.5 V; link ECC; DVFS/DVFSC; deep sleep; Data-Copy / Write-X; CKE eliminated; up to 6400 Mbps.
Speed up to 8533 Mbit/s; tx/rx equalization; Adaptive Refresh Management.
Successor; CA bus narrowed further; 12-bit data bus per channel; higher speeds. Out of scope of JESD209-5.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: New clocking architecture: quarter-speed CK + on-demand full-speed WCK + DRAM-driven RDQS
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: WCK/RDQS enabled only when needed -> major IO power saving; requires WCK2CK sync before every high-speed transfer.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: CA bus widened to 7 bits, double data rate
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: Commands arrive at the same cadence as LPDDR4 despite quarter-speed CK; a command spans two CA transfers.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: CAS command moved before the read/write (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR)
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: CAS synchronizes WCK to CK (does not select a column), unlike LPDDR4's trailing CAS-2.
Bank-group timing enables concurrency; 16n prefetch retained (NOT doubled).
Lower IO power; DFE + (5B) tx/rx equalization required for SI.
On-the-wire single-bit correction; reduced driven-bit count.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: DVFS / DVFSC, deep sleep, Data-Copy / Write-X
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: Fine-grained power scaling and data-transfer reduction.
Low-power entry is a CA command bounded by CS.

fields.version_naming_history_note: DDR5 SDRAM is standardized by JEDEC as JESD79-5, the fifth generation in the JESD79 mainstream DDR family (DDR -> DDR2 -> DDR3 -> DDR4 -> DDR5). Each generation roughly doubles peak data rate while lowering the supply voltage. DDR5's defining additions over DDR4 (JESD79-4) are the two independent sub-channels, DFE, on-die ECC, same-bank refresh, BL16, internal VrefDQ/VrefCA, the 2-cycle CA protocol, and the DIMM PMIC/SPD-hub/RCD module architecture.

spec_lineage_hbm.summary: First HBM; 1.0 Gb/s/pin; 1024-bit; up to 4 GB/stack; ~128 GB/s.
HBM2; 8 channels of 128 bits; up to 8 GB/stack; ~256-307 GB/s.
Up to 3.2-3.6 Gb/s/pin; up to 307 GB/s/stack; 12-Hi for 24 GB.
16 channels of 64 bits (1024-bit total); up to 6.4 Gb/s/pin; up to 819 GB/s/stack; 8-Hi (16 GB) / 12-Hi (24 GB) of 16 Gb dies; on-die + link ECC; RFM; RAS.
2048-bit interface; up to 8 Gb/s/pin; up to 2 TB/s; backwards compatible with HBM3 controllers.

key_changes_vs_hbm2e.impact: Finer access granularity; total still 1024 data pins.

key_changes_vs_hbm2e.change: Per-pin rate doubled to 6.4 Gb/s/pin (vs JEDEC HBM2E 3.2)
key_changes_vs_hbm2e.impact: Up to 819 GB/s per stack vs ~307.
Independent column streams per channel half.

key_changes_vs_hbm2e.change: 12-Hi stacks of 16 Gb dies (~30 µm thick) for 24 GB

previous_versions: DDR3 (JESD79-3) — 1.5 V, DLL, 8n prefetch, single 64/72-bit bus, BL8.
DDR4 (JESD79-4) — 1.2 V, bank groups, single 64/72-bit bus, BL8, gear-down.

key_changes_vs_ddr4.summary: Each DIMM is split into two independent 32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels (DDR4: single 64/72-bit bus).
Decision Feedback Equalization (DFE) on DQ receivers and a Duty-Cycle Adjuster (DDR4: none).
On-die ECC standard in every device plus Error Check and Scrub (DDR4: not standard).
32 banks in 8 bank groups and same-bank refresh (REFsb) (DDR4: 16 banks / 4 groups, no REFsb).
Internal VrefDQ/VrefCA with CA/read/write training (DDR4: external VrefDQ in many configurations).
DIMM-level PMIC, SPD hub, and RCD (DDR4: motherboard power, simpler SPD).
